supporting_observations.claim: The closest recorded PowerShell activity to the reported time begins at 13:45:25 on WS-ACOLE-01 under sean.byrne and runs the documented Patch-Workstations.ps1 script from FILE-ORC-01.

The activity is consistent with scheduled workstation patching: sean.byrne authenticated from WS-SBYRNE-01 shortly beforehand, and the PowerShell process initiated a Windows Update download followed by wusa installing a Windows update package.
At 13:40:20, the recorded process launch on WS-ACOLE-01 was GlobalProtect's PanGPA.exe, not PowerShell.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied process records do not establish what window Amy saw or whether it was visible to her; they record process creation and execution, not the user's screen.

The nearest recorded PowerShell launch is at 13:45:25, several minutes after the reported approximate time; the evidence does not establish that this was the exact window Amy reported. The records show the launch time and command line, but not a direct link to the report. (T264-00246, T264-00247)
claims_not_established: Whether the reported window appeared at exactly 13:40 or whether Amy's approximate time included the 13:45 patch activity. (T264-00191, T264-00246)
Whether the patch script displayed a PowerShell window to Amy; the process records do not establish visibility. (T264-00246, T264-00247)
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: Amy launched PowerShell at 13:54:47 to enumerate scheduled tasks, then launched sqlcmd with a command to back up the reporting database to D:\Backups\inventory.bak. These events occur well after the reported time and are not used to decide this alert. (T264-00274, T264-00305, T264-00320)
